extracted.intended_audience: research funders, program officers, peer review administrators, scientometricians, and policy researchers interested in grant evaluation
extracted.subtask_description: Use bibliometric measures to evaluate whether peer review scores predict subsequent research impact and to inform funding strategy decisions (award size, number funded, portfolio balance). Analysis uses retrospective grant-level data and citation-based impact metrics over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correlation between peer review scores and bibliometric output
rubrics_metrics.description: “Peer review scores associated with applications were found to be moderately correlated with the total time-adjusted citation output of funded projects, although a high degree of variability existed in the data.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use statistical correlation between application peer review scores and subsequent citation-based output to assess predictive validity of peer review. Expect moderate correlation but substantial scatter; interpret results acknowledging variability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Total Relative Citation (TRC) per application as impact metric
rubrics_metrics.description: TRC is defined as the summation of all citations from individual grant publication yield normalized against the Reuters average (referred to as average Total Relative Citations (TRC) per funded application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure impact at the application level using summed, field-normalized citations (TRC). Present TRC per application, average TRC by score group, and total annual TRC for program-level assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-adjust citation counts (time-adjusted citation output)
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses use total time-adjusted citation output to account for differences in citation accrual over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust citation measures for time since publication (or funding year) so older projects' higher raw citation counts do not bias correlations. Use time-normalized or age-adjusted citation indicators when linking peer review scores to impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average Annual Score (AAS) trend analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Average application score of all applications submitted in a given review year (AAS) was calculated and plotted over time; as AAS improved over time, average annual citation output per application increased.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track changes in mean application quality (AAS) across years and compare to mean annual TRC to detect temporal trends in application quality and impact; fit linear regressions to evaluate trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total annual TRC vs number of funded applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of funded applications per year was found to correlate well with total annual citation impact (total annual TRC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess program-level impact by summing TRC across funded projects per year and test correlation with count of awards. This supports evaluating strategies that change the number of awards (e.g., smaller awards to more investigators).

rubrics_metrics.name: Award size and program budget are not predictive of citation impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Citation impact did not correlate with the amount of funds awarded per application or with the total annual programmatic budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume larger per-award funding or larger program budgets will increase citation-based impact. Empirically test whether reallocating funds (e.g., smaller awards to more applicants) affects total impact, while controlling for confounders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider portfolio balance and high-cost research areas when changing award sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: The strategy of improving funding success rates by reducing the size of awards to fund more applications must be weighed against the need for a balanced research portfolio and the inherent high costs of some areas of research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When optimizing for citation impact, include qualitative/programmatic constraints: portfolio diversity, strategic priorities, and disciplines with inherently higher costs or lower citation dynamics may warrant larger awards despite potential impact trade-offs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping applications by review score for group-level analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications were grouped by identical review score and then averaged (average TRC values plotted for the 21 scoring groups); these average TRC values were fit with a linear function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform score-group analyses (aggregate by identical or binned scores) to reduce noise at the individual-application level and to evaluate the trend of impact across score bands. Report group sample sizes and standard errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: High variability and stochasticity in peer review outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: A high degree of variability existed in the data (and prior literature documents a high degree of chance associated with funding), indicating substantial unpredictability in which proposals yield high citation impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret correlations cautiously, acknowledging random effects and reviewer disagreement; consider complementary evaluation approaches and prospective testing to better understand sources of variability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for prospective model systems to test peer review formats and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The relationship observed between peer review scores and bibliometric output lays the groundwork for establishing a model system for future prospective testing of the validity of peer review formats and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design prospective, possibly randomized or controlled, evaluations of peer review formats (scoring systems, panel structures, funding allocation rules) using predefined bibliometric and other impact endpoints to validate and improve peer review processes.
